database_investigation.interpretation: Entity-encoded content is indexed as its markup rather than the rendered accented word in this fixture. This establishes a database-level mismatch, not whether all Unicode search or all editors are affected. Server defaults are not proof of table/column collation.

ordinary_word_check.interpretation: An isolated temporary MyISAM full-text table reproduced the 50% natural-language threshold: with revised in one of two rows, natural score was zero while boolean matched; adding one unrelated row made the natural score positive, with boolean still matching. This explains the observed failure on the two-row fixture table. This is separate from entity-encoded text.

isolated_threshold_test.cleanup: temporary table automatically dropped when database session ended

ranking_comparison.interpretation: At the 50% threshold natural-language ignores both common terms; boolean mode finds both matching rows but assigns equal scores despite one row repeating revised. This small example demonstrates that switching search modes affects relevance behavior and requires broader tests. A separate row containing literal café and café matched both café and eacute respectively in boolean mode.

fallback_experiment.strategy: Filter using boolean full-text, order by natural-language score, then boolean score and id.
fallback_experiment.limitations: Isolated SQL experiment only; Composr translated and non-translated query paths, pagination, permissions, cross-database behavior, query semantics and performance remain untested. Does not address HTML entity indexing.
